Why we're here.

The problem

Most companies stitch four or five tools together.

Lead capture in one place. Field sales in another. Service in a third. Payroll bolted on. The customer feels every seam.

Tool 1

CRM

Lives in one place. Owns contact records.

Tool 2

Field sales

Different tool. Different login. Notes don't sync.

Tool 3

Service mgmt

Third tool. Limited scope. Wrapped with custom.

Tool 4

Payroll

Spreadsheets. Manual reconciliation. Errors at scale.

What the customer feels

Every seam.

The hand-off lag. The retyped name. The "we'll get back to you." The repeated questions across teams. The relationship dies between handoffs.

The Accountability Engine

Work routes by event. Beta

The system answers four questions on every job: Who sold it? Who installed it? Did the install complete? Did the customer get the outcome we promised? Accountability — and the audit trail HD can ask for — follows the same path.

1 · Sold?Setter and closer attribution captured at the sale.
2 · Installed?Installer attribution captured at completion.
3 · Completed?Step-gated workflow confirms install actually finished.
4 · Collected?Revenue collected signals pay routing eligibility.
In scope · Beta

Preview, commission logic, QA, export support.

  • Payroll preview by rep, by team, by period
  • Commission logic configurable per role
  • QA pass against test-rep data before any live use
  • Export to the existing payroll system
Out of scope today · Roadmap

Live disbursement.

  • Live pay-out behind verified math against test reps
  • Test-rep guardrails: never run against Josh / Luke real accounts
  • Manual adjustment column for one-offs (gas, bonus)
  • Reimbursement OCR for installer receipts
Care note: Same engine drives internal commission logic. HD never sees pay numbers — only the accountability signal: who owns each step.

Role Architecture
